passages.text: After this, the Lord appointed seventy-two others and sent them two by two ahead of Him to every town and place He was about to visit.
passages.sermon:
The Lord chose seventy-two other people.
He appointed them for a special task.
He sent them out in pairs.
He sent them ahead of Him.
He sent them to every town and place.
He planned to visit these towns and places Himself.
passages.original: Μετὰ δὲ ταῦτα ἀνέδειξεν ὁ Κύριος καὶ ἑτέρους ἑβδομήκοντα δύο καὶ ἀπέστειλεν αὐτοὺς ἀνὰ δύο δύο πρὸ προσώπου αὐτοῦ εἰς πᾶσαν πόλιν καὶ τόπον οὗ ἤμελλεν αὐτὸς ἔρχεσθαι

passages.text: And He told them, “The harvest is plentiful, but the workers are few. Ask the Lord of the harvest, therefore, to send out workers into His harvest.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His followers.
He said, “The harvest is plentiful.
But the workers are few.
Pray to the Lord of the harvest.
Ask Him to send workers into His harvest.”
passages.original: ἔλεγεν δὲ πρὸς αὐτούς Ὁ μὲν θερισμὸς πολύς οἱ δὲ ἐργάται ὀλίγοι δεήθητε οὖν τοῦ Κυρίου τοῦ θερισμοῦ ὅπως ἐργάτας ἐκβάλῃ εἰς τὸν θερισμὸν αὐτοῦ

passages.text: Go! I am sending you out like lambs among wolves.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Lord.
Jesus spoke to the seventy-two people He appointed.
Jesus said, "Go."
Jesus said, "I am sending you out."
Jesus said, "You are like lambs."
Jesus said, "You are among wolves."
passages.original: Ὑπάγετε ἰδοὺ ἀποστέλλω ὑμᾶς ὡς ἄρνας ἐν μέσῳ λύκων

passages.text: Carry no purse or bag or sandals. Do not greet anyone along the road.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He gave them instructions for their mission.
He said, "Do not carry a purse."
He said, "Do not carry a bag."
He said, "Do not wear sandals."
He said, "Do not greet anyone along the road."
passages.original: μὴ βαστάζετε βαλλάντιον μὴ πήραν μὴ ὑποδήματα καὶ μηδένα κατὰ τὴν ὁδὸν ἀσπάσησθε

passages.text: Whatever house you enter, begin by saying, ‘Peace to this house.’
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to his disciples.
\r\nHe sent them out to preach.
\r\nHe told them what to do when they entered a house.
\r\nWhenever you enter a house, speak first.
\r\nSay, “Peace to this house.”
passages.original: Εἰς ἣν δ’ ἂν εἰσέλθητε οἰκίαν πρῶτον λέγετε Εἰρήνη τῷ οἴκῳ τούτῳ

passages.text: If a man of peace is there, your peace will rest on him; if not, it will return to you.
passages.sermon:
Jesus sent his followers to visit houses.
He told them to greet each house with peace.
If a peaceful person lives there, your peace will rest on him.
If there is no peaceful person, your peace will return to you.
passages.original: καὶ ἐὰν ἐκεῖ ᾖ υἱὸς εἰρήνης ἐπαναπαήσεται ἐπ’ αὐτὸν ἡ εἰρήνη ὑμῶν εἰ δὲ μή¦γε ἐφ’ ὑμᾶς ἀνακάμψει

passages.text: Stay at the same house, eating and drinking whatever you are offered. For the worker is worthy of his wages. Do not move around from house to house.
passages.sermon:
Jesus sent out his followers to preach and heal.
He gave them instructions for their journey.
He told them to stay in the same house when they entered a town.
He told them to eat and drink whatever the people in that house gave them.
He said the worker deserves his wages.
He told them not to move from one house to another.
passages.original: ἐν αὐτῇ δὲ τῇ οἰκίᾳ μένετε ἐσθίοντες καὶ πίνοντες τὰ παρ’ αὐτῶν ἄξιος γὰρ ὁ ἐργάτης τοῦ μισθοῦ αὐτοῦ μὴ μεταβαίνετε ἐξ οἰκίας εἰς οἰκίαν

passages.text: If you enter a town and they welcome you, eat whatever is set before you.
passages.sermon:
Jesus sent out his followers to preach and heal.
He gave them instructions for their journey.
If you enter a town and the people welcome you, stay there.
Eat whatever food they give you.
passages.original: Καὶ εἰς ἣν ἂν πόλιν εἰσέρχησθε καὶ δέχωνται ὑμᾶς ἐσθίετε τὰ παρατιθέμενα ὑμῖν

passages.text: Heal the sick who are there and tell them, ‘The kingdom of God is near you.’
passages.sermon:
Jesus sent his followers to different towns.
He told them to heal the sick people in each town.
He told them to speak to the people.
He told them to say, “The kingdom of God is near you.”
passages.original: καὶ θεραπεύετε τοὺς ἐν αὐτῇ ἀσθενεῖς καὶ λέγετε αὐτοῖς Ἤγγικεν ἐφ’ ὑμᾶς ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ Θεοῦ

passages.text: But if you enter a town and they do not welcome you, go into the streets and declare, ‘Even the dust of your town that clings to our feet, we wipe off as a testimony against you. Yet be sure of this: The kingdom of God is near.’
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to his followers.
He sent them to different towns.
He told them what to do if people did not welcome them.
If you enter a town and the people do not welcome you, go into the streets.
Say to them, “We wipe off even the dust of your town that sticks to our feet.”
This shows we are leaving you behind.
But know this: The kingdom of God is near.
passages.original: Εἰς ἣν δ’ ἂν πόλιν εἰσέλθητε καὶ μὴ δέχωνται ὑμᾶς ἐξελθόντες εἰς τὰς πλατείας αὐτῆς εἴπατε Καὶ τὸν κονιορτὸν τὸν κολληθέντα ἡμῖν ἐκ τῆς πόλεως ὑμῶν εἰς τοὺς πόδας ἀπομασσόμεθα ὑμῖν πλὴν τοῦτο γινώσκετε ὅτι ἤγγικεν ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ Θεοῦ

passages.text: I tell you, it will be more bearable on that day for Sodom than for that town.
passages.sermon:
Jesus speaks to His disciples.
He warns about judgment for those who reject His message.
He says, “I tell you the truth.
On that day of judgment, Sodom will have it easier than that town.”
passages.original: λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι Σοδόμοις ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἐκείνῃ ἀνεκτότερον ἔσται ἢ τῇ πόλει ἐκείνῃ

passages.text: Woe to you, Chorazin! Woe to you, Bethsaida! For if the miracles that were performed in you had been performed in Tyre and Sidon, they would have repented long ago, sitting in sackcloth and ashes.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people of Chorazin and Bethsaida.
He said, “Woe to you, Chorazin.
Woe to you, Bethsaida.
I did miracles in Chorazin and Bethsaida.
If I had done these miracles in Tyre and Sidon, the people there would have repented long ago.
They would have sat in sackcloth and ashes to show their sorrow and repentance.”
passages.original: Οὐαί σοι Χοραζίν οὐαί σοι Βηθσαϊδά ὅτι εἰ ἐν Τύρῳ καὶ Σιδῶνι ἐγενήθησαν αἱ δυνάμεις αἱ γενόμεναι ἐν ὑμῖν πάλαι ἂν ἐν σάκκῳ καὶ σποδῷ καθήμενοι μετενόησαν

passages.text: But it will be more bearable for Tyre and Sidon at the judgment than for you.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people of Chorazin and Bethsaida.
He compared them to the cities of Tyre and Sidon.
Jesus said a day of judgment will come.
On that day, Tyre and Sidon will face judgment.
It will be easier for Tyre and Sidon than for Chorazin and Bethsaida.
Chorazin and Bethsaida will face a harder judgment.
passages.original: πλὴν Τύρῳ καὶ Σιδῶνι ἀνεκτότερον ἔσται ἐν τῇ κρίσει ἢ ὑμῖν

passages.text: And you, Capernaum, will you be lifted up to heaven? No, you will be brought down to Hades!
passages.sermon: Capernaum, you are a city.\r\nYou will not be lifted up to heaven.\r\nYou will be brought down to Hades.
passages.original: καὶ σύ Καφαρναούμ μὴ ἕως οὐρανοῦ ὑψωθήσῃ ἕως τοῦ ᾅδου καταβήσῃ

passages.text: Whoever listens to you listens to Me; whoever rejects you rejects Me; and whoever rejects Me rejects the One who sent Me.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He said, “Whoever listens to you listens to Me.
Whoever rejects you rejects Me.
Whoever rejects Me rejects the One who sent Me.”
passages.original: Ὁ ἀκούων ὑμῶν ἐμοῦ ἀκούει καὶ ὁ ἀθετῶν ὑμᾶς ἐμὲ ἀθετεῖ ὁ δὲ ἐμὲ ἀθετῶν ἀθετεῖ τὸν ἀποστείλαντά με

passages.text: The seventy-two returned with joy and said, “Lord, even the demons submit to us in Your name.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus sent out seventy-two followers.
These followers returned to Jesus.
They felt great joy.
They spoke to Jesus.
They said, “Lord, even the demons obey us.”
They said, “They obey us when we use Your name.”
passages.original: Ὑπέστρεψαν δὲ οἱ ἑβδομήκοντα δύο μετὰ χαρᾶς λέγοντες Κύριε καὶ τὰ δαιμόνια ὑποτάσσεται ἡμῖν ἐν τῷ ὀνόματί σου

passages.text: So He told them, “I saw Satan fall like lightning from heaven.
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke to the seventy-two disciples.\r\nJesus said, “I saw Satan fall from heaven.\r\nSatan fell like lightning.”
passages.original: Εἶπεν δὲ αὐτοῖς Ἐθεώρουν τὸν Σατανᾶν ὡς ἀστραπὴν ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ πεσόντα

passages.text: Behold, I have given you authority to tread on snakes and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy. Nothing will harm you.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the seventy-two disciples.
Jesus gave them authority.
They could walk on snakes.
They could walk on scorpions.
They had power over all the enemy’s strength.
Nothing would harm them.
passages.original: ἰδοὺ δέδωκα ὑμῖν τὴν ἐξουσίαν τοῦ πατεῖν ἐπάνω ὄφεων καὶ σκορπίων καὶ ἐπὶ πᾶσαν τὴν δύναμιν τοῦ ἐχθροῦ καὶ οὐδὲν ὑμᾶς οὐ μὴ ἀδικήσῃ

passages.text: Nevertheless, do not rejoice that the spirits submit to you, but rejoice that your names are written in heaven.”
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke to His disciples.\r\nHe told them not to rejoice because spirits submit to them.\r\nHe told them to rejoice because God has written their names in heaven.
passages.original: πλὴν ἐν τούτῳ μὴ χαίρετε ὅτι τὰ πνεύματα ὑμῖν ὑποτάσσεται χαίρετε δὲ ὅτι τὰ ὀνόματα ὑμῶν ἐνγέγραπται ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς

passages.text: At that time Jesus rejoiced in the Holy Spirit and declared, “I praise You, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because You have hidden these things from the wise and learned, and revealed them to little children. Yes, Father, for this was well-pleasing in Your sight.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Son of God.
At that time, Jesus felt great joy in the Holy Spirit.
Jesus spoke to God the Father.
God is the Lord of heaven and earth.
Jesus said, “Father, I praise You.
You have hidden these things from people who are wise and learned.
You have shown these things to little children.
Yes, Father, this pleased You.”
passages.original: Ἐν αὐτῇ τῇ ὥρᾳ ἠγαλλιάσατο ἐν τῷ Πνεύματι τῷ Ἁγίῳ καὶ εἶπεν Ἐξομολογοῦμαί σοι Πάτερ Κύριε τοῦ οὐρανοῦ καὶ τῆς γῆς ὅτι ἀπέκρυψας ταῦτα ἀπὸ σοφῶν καὶ συνετῶν καὶ ἀπεκάλυψας αὐτὰ νηπίοις ναί ὁ Πατήρ ὅτι οὕτως εὐδοκία ἐγένετο ἔμπροσθέν σου

passages.text: All things have been entrusted to Me by My Father. No one knows who the Son is except the Father, and no one knows who the Father is except the Son and those to whom the Son chooses to reveal Him.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
Jesus is the Son of God.
God is the Father of Jesus.
The Father has given everything to Jesus.
Only the Father truly knows who the Son is.
Only the Son truly knows who the Father is.
The Son can reveal the Father to anyone He chooses.
passages.original: Πάντα μοι παρεδόθη ὑπὸ τοῦ Πατρός μου καὶ οὐδεὶς γινώσκει τίς ἐστιν ὁ Υἱὸς εἰ μὴ ὁ Πατήρ καὶ τίς ἐστιν ὁ Πατὴρ εἰ μὴ ὁ Υἱὸς καὶ ᾧ ἐὰν βούληται ὁ Υἱὸς ἀποκαλύψαι

passages.text: Then Jesus turned to the disciples and said privately, “Blessed are the eyes that see what you see.
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke to His disciples in private.\r\nHe turned to them.\r\nHe said, “Blessed are the eyes that see what you see.”
passages.original: Καὶ στραφεὶς πρὸς τοὺς μαθητὰς κατ’ ἰδίαν εἶπεν Μακάριοι οἱ ὀφθαλμοὶ οἱ βλέποντες ἃ βλέπετε

passages.text: For I tell you that many prophets and kings desired to see what you see but did not see it, and to hear what you hear but did not hear it.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
Jesus said, “Many prophets wanted to see what you see.
Many kings also wanted to see what you see.
They did not see it.
Many prophets wanted to hear what you hear.
Many kings also wanted to hear what you hear.
They did not hear it.”
passages.original: λέγω γὰρ ὑμῖν ὅτι πολλοὶ προφῆται καὶ βασιλεῖς ἠθέλησαν ἰδεῖν ἃ ὑμεῖς βλέπετε καὶ οὐκ εἶδαν καὶ ἀκοῦσαι ἃ ἀκούετε καὶ οὐκ ἤκουσαν

passages.text: One day an expert in the law stood up to test Him. “Teacher,” he asked, “what must I do to inherit eternal life?”
passages.sermon:
An expert in the law stood up.
He wanted to test Jesus.
He spoke to Jesus.
He said, “Teacher, what must I do to inherit eternal life?”
passages.original: Καὶ ἰδοὺ νομικός τις ἀνέστη ἐκπειράζων αὐτὸν λέγων Διδάσκαλε τί ποιήσας ζωὴν αἰώνιον κληρονομήσω

passages.text: “What is written in the Law?” Jesus replied. “How do you read it?”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the expert in the law.
Jesus asked him a question.
Jesus said, “What is written in the Law?”
Jesus also said, “How do you read it?”
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτόν Ἐν τῷ νόμῳ τί γέγραπται πῶς ἀναγινώσκεις

passages.text: He answered, “ ‘Love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your strength and with all your mind’ and ‘Love your neighbor as yourself.’”
passages.sermon:
An expert in the law spoke to Jesus.
He answered Jesus’ question.
He said, “Love the Lord your God.”
Love God with all your heart.
Love God with all your soul.
Love God with all your strength.
Love God with all your mind.
Love your neighbor as yourself.”
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν Ἀγαπήσεις Κύριον τὸν Θεόν σου ἐξ ὅλης τῆς καρδίας σου καὶ ἐν ὅλῃ τῇ ψυχῇ σου καὶ ἐν ὅλῃ τῇ ἰσχύϊ σου καὶ ἐν ὅλῃ τῇ διανοίᾳ σου καὶ Τὸν πλησίον σου ὡς σεαυτόν

passages.text: “You have answered correctly,” Jesus said. “Do this and you will live.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the man.
Jesus said, “You have answered correctly.”
Jesus said, “Do this.”
Jesus said, “You will live.”
passages.original: Εἶπεν δὲ αὐτῷ Ὀρθῶς ἀπεκρίθης τοῦτο ποίει καὶ ζήσῃ

passages.text: But wanting to justify himself, he asked Jesus, “And who is my neighbor?”
passages.sermon:
A man spoke to Jesus.
This man wanted to justify himself.
He asked Jesus a question.
He said, “Who is my neighbor?”
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ θέλων δικαιῶσαι ἑαυτὸν εἶπεν πρὸς τὸν Ἰησοῦν Καὶ τίς ἐστίν μου πλησίον

passages.text: Jesus took up this question and said, “A man was going down from Jerusalem to Jericho when he fell into the hands of robbers. They stripped him, beat him, and went away, leaving him half dead.
passages.sermon:
Jesus answered the question.
He told a story.
A man was traveling from Jerusalem to Jericho.
Robbers attacked him.
The robbers took his clothes.
They beat him.
They left him.
He was half dead.
passages.original: Ὑπολαβὼν δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν Ἄνθρωπός τις κατέβαινεν ἀπὸ Ἰερουσαλὴμ εἰς Ἰεριχὼ καὶ λῃσταῖς περιέπεσεν οἳ καὶ ἐκδύσαντες αὐτὸν καὶ πληγὰς ἐπιθέντες ἀπῆλθον ἀφέντες ἡμιθανῆ

passages.text: Now by chance a priest was going down the same road, but when he saw him, he passed by on the other side.
passages.sermon:
A priest was traveling down that road.
He came by chance.
He saw the injured man.
He passed by on the other side.
passages.original: Κατὰ συγκυρίαν δὲ ἱερεύς τις κατέβαινεν ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ ἐκείνῃ καὶ ἰδὼν αὐτὸν ἀντιπαρῆλθεν

passages.text: So too, when a Levite came to that spot and saw him, he passed by on the other side.
passages.sermon:
A Levite walked to that place.
He saw the injured man.
The Levite did not stop.
He passed by on the other side of the road.
passages.original: Ὁμοίως δὲ καὶ Λευίτης γενόμενος κατὰ τὸν τόπον ἐλθὼν καὶ ἰδὼν ἀντιπαρῆλθεν

passages.text: But when a Samaritan on a journey came upon him, he looked at him and had compassion.
passages.sermon: A Samaritan was traveling on the road.\r\nHe saw the injured man.\r\nThe Samaritan felt compassion for him.
passages.original: Σαμαρίτης δέ τις ὁδεύων ἦλθεν κατ’ αὐτὸν καὶ ἰδὼν ἐσπλαγχνίσθη

passages.text: He went to him and bandaged his wounds, pouring on oil and wine. Then he put him on his own animal, brought him to an inn, and took care of him.
passages.sermon:
A Samaritan saw the injured man.
The Samaritan went to the man.
He bandaged the man's wounds.
He poured oil and wine on the wounds.
He put the man on his own animal.
He brought the man to an inn.
He took care of the man.
passages.original: καὶ προσελθὼν κατέδησεν τὰ τραύματα αὐτοῦ ἐπιχέων ἔλαιον καὶ οἶνον ἐπιβιβάσας δὲ αὐτὸν ἐπὶ τὸ ἴδιον κτῆνος ἤγαγεν αὐτὸν εἰς πανδοχεῖον καὶ ἐπεμελήθη αὐτοῦ

passages.text: The next day he took out two denarii and gave them to the innkeeper. ‘Take care of him,’ he said, ‘and on my return I will repay you for any additional expense.’
passages.sermon:
The Samaritan helped a wounded man.
The next day, the Samaritan took out two denarii.
He gave the two denarii to the innkeeper.
The Samaritan spoke to the innkeeper.
He said, "Take care of him."
He also said, "If you spend anything more, I will repay you when I return."
passages.original: Καὶ ἐπὶ τὴν αὔριον ἐκβαλὼν δύο δηνάρια ἔδωκεν τῷ πανδοχεῖ καὶ εἶπεν Ἐπιμελήθητι αὐτοῦ καὶ ὅ τι ἂν προσδαπανήσῃς ἐγὼ ἐν τῷ ἐπανέρχεσθαί με ἀποδώσω σοι

passages.text: Which of these three do you think was a neighbor to the man who fell into the hands of robbers?”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to an expert in the law.
A man had fallen into the hands of robbers.
Three people saw the man.
Jesus asked a question.
He said, "Which of these three was a neighbor to the man who fell among robbers?"
passages.original: Τίς τούτων τῶν τριῶν πλησίον δοκεῖ σοι γεγονέναι τοῦ ἐμπεσόντος εἰς τοὺς λῃστάς

passages.text: “The one who showed him mercy,” replied the expert in the law. Then Jesus told him, “Go and do likewise.”
passages.sermon:
An expert in the law spoke to Jesus.
The expert answered a question from Jesus.
He said, “The one who showed him mercy.”
Jesus spoke to the expert.
Jesus said, “Go and do likewise.”
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ εἶπεν Ὁ ποιήσας τὸ ἔλεος μετ’ αὐτοῦ Εἶπεν δὲ αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς Πορεύου καὶ σὺ ποίει ὁμοίως

passages.text: As they traveled along, Jesus entered a village where a woman named Martha welcomed Him into her home.
passages.sermon:
Jesus traveled with His followers.
Jesus entered a village.
A woman named Martha lived in that village.
Martha welcomed Jesus into her home.
passages.original: Ἐν δὲ τῷ πορεύεσθαι αὐτοὺς αὐτὸς εἰσῆλθεν εἰς κώμην τινά γυνὴ δέ τις ὀνόματι Μάρθα ὑπεδέξατο αὐτὸν εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν

passages.text: She had a sister named Mary, who sat at the Lord’s feet listening to His message.
passages.sermon:
Martha had a sister.
Her sister’s name was Mary.
Mary sat at the feet of the Lord Jesus.
Mary listened to the words of Jesus.
passages.original: καὶ τῇδε ἦν ἀδελφὴ καλουμένη Μαριάμ ἣ καὶ παρακαθεσθεῖσα πρὸς τοὺς πόδας τοῦ Κυρίου ἤκουεν τὸν λόγον αὐτοῦ

passages.text: But Martha was distracted by all the preparations to be made. She came to Jesus and said, “Lord, do You not care that my sister has left me to serve alone? Tell her to help me!”
passages.sermon:
Martha was a woman who welcomed Jesus into her home.
Martha became distracted by many preparations.
Martha went to Jesus.
Martha spoke to Jesus.
She said, “Lord, do you not care?”
She said, “My sister has left me to serve alone.”
She said, “Tell her to help me.”
passages.original: ἡ δὲ Μάρθα περιεσπᾶτο περὶ πολλὴν διακονίαν ἐπιστᾶσα δὲ εἶπεν Κύριε οὐ μέλει σοι ὅτι ἡ ἀδελφή μου μόνην με κατέλειπεν διακονεῖν εἰπὲ οὖν αὐτῇ ἵνα μοι συναντιλάβηται

passages.text: “Martha, Martha,” the Lord replied, “you are worried and upset about many things.
passages.sermon:
Jesus was present in the house of two sisters, Martha and Mary.
Martha was busy with many tasks.
Mary sat at Jesus’ feet and listened to Him.
Martha spoke to Jesus about her concerns.
The Lord answered Martha.
He said, “Martha, Martha, you are worried about many things.
You are upset about many things.”
passages.original: Ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ εἶπεν αὐτῇ ὁ Κύριος Μάρθα Μάρθα μεριμνᾷς καὶ θορυβάζῃ περὶ πολλά

passages.text: But only one thing is necessary. Mary has chosen the good portion, and it will not be taken away from her.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to Martha.
Jesus said that only one thing is truly necessary.
Mary chose what is good.
No one will take this good thing away from Mary.
passages.original: ὀλίγων δέ ἐστιν χρεία ἢ ἑνός Μαριὰμ γὰρ τὴν ἀγαθὴν μερίδα ἐξελέξατο ἥτις οὐκ ἀφαιρεθήσεται αὐτῆς
